column1: ## without learning Verify's application JSON.
## Column mapping onto Verify's POST /v1.0/applications body:
##   name             -> name  (the application's display name in the console)
##   role             -> which demo job this client does; drives the defaults
##                       below. One of: mint | exchange | audience
##   ropc             -> providers.oidc.properties.grantTypes.ropc
##   client_creds     -> providers.oidc.properties.grantTypes.clientCredentials
##   token_exchange   -> providers.oidc.properties.grantTypes.tokenExchange
##   audiences        -> providers.oidc.token.audiences        (pipe-separated)
##   claims           -> providers.oidc.token.attributeMappings (pipe-separated;
##                       each becomes a CELx mapper — see import-verify-clients.sh)
##   pdv_id_key       -> where the generated client_id is written back into
##   pdv_secret_key      post_deploy_variables.json (blank = do not write back)
## Grant-type cells are true/false and become the QUOTED strings Verify requires.
## An empty audiences/claims cell means "none".
## Why four rows when Verify only needs two clients
## The Keycloak realm has four clients. Only two of them are real OAuth clients
## on Verify:
##   hr-copilot     mints user + client tokens (ROPC + client_credentials)
##   praxis-gateway performs the RFC 8693 exchange
## They must stay distinct: Verify refuses to let a client exchange its own
## tokens (CSIAQ5207E)
column2: the same split the realm export already has.

column1: ## github-api and workday-api are NOT clients on Verify — they are audience
## STRINGS in the exchange client's `audiences` list (see delta V1 in
## docs/brainstorms/2026-08-31-ibm-verify-idp-requirements.md). They are
## registered here as `role=audience` so this file mirrors the realm export
## 1:1 and the console shows the same four names a viewer sees in Keycloak.
## Three things registering them does NOT do:
##   - it does not make Verify honor a requested `audience` (delta V1: Verify
##     stamps the exchanging client's fixed list and accepts unregistered
##     audiences silently);
##   - it does not reproduce Keycloak's per-audience `gh-permissions-as-scope`
##     mapper
